text:
morgan: heads up — customer hit a build-time failure when using the SDK from a Next.js middleware on Vercel Edge: "Cannot find module '@redwood/inference/edge' or its corresponding type declarations"

tay: quick guess: package has conditional exports for runtime but we didn't point types at the edge subpath. TS will look at types field and can miss subpath types.

sam: confirmed locally. runtime import works via dynamic import, but tsc/VSCode can't resolve the types because exports map lacks a `types` entry for `./edge`.

ben: minimal fix: add `exports: {"./edge": {"import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs","types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts"}, ".": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.mjs","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs","types":"./dist/esm/index.d.ts"}}` and publish. Also add a tiny edge entry that avoids node shims and provides a default export for plain JS.

morgan: note: Next's SWC sometimes rewrites imports and strips some globals. the edge entry must assume global fetch/Request/Response and not import node polyfills.

tay: CI suggestion: add a job that installs the package into a fixture Next app, runs `tsc --noEmit` and `next build` to catch both type and bundling issues. also run `node -e "import('@redwood/inference/edge').then(console.log)"` in node 18 to ensure subpath import resolves.

sam: docs: include three concise examples: 1) recommended edge pattern (dynamic import from `@redwood/inference/edge`), 2) JS-friendly default import, 3) fallback CommonJS for node servers. add note about esbuild target es2020+ and not including node polyfills.

jira-bot: Created SDK-2145: add edge types & edge entry + CI checks. Assigned to sam.

morgan: thanks all — I'll add the snippet to the support KB and link the PR once it's up. :thumbsup:
